payload.title: Week of Nov 16, 2026
payload.headline: Tech (QQQ) in a downtrend, broad market (SPY) sideways, fear normal.

verdict.text: QQQ fell 1.2% and stays below its 50-day average: the downtrend continues. No setup is approved: 5 live setups are blocked, most often by "QQQ is not above its 50-day average". Nothing has a proven edge, so the default is no action. Next decision points: NVDA earnings Nov 17; GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 Nov 25 08:30; Personal Income and Outlays, October 2026 (includes PCE inflation) Nov 25 08:30.

items.text: S&P 500 (SPY): $757.12 → $754.37 (2026-11-13). Down 0.4% on the day. Above its 200-day but below its 50-day average: the long trend holds, the short trend is broken.
Nasdaq-100 (QQQ): $688.17 → $679.89 (2026-11-13). Down 1.2% on the day. Below its 50- and 200-day averages: the trend is down.
VIX (fear gauge): 18.70 → 19.30 (2026-11-13). Fear normal. Little changed.
10-year Treasury yield: 4.98% → 5.10% (2026-11-12). Little changed over 4 weeks.
Breadth (tracked tech above 50-day): — → 25.00% (2026-11-13). Few stocks are taking part: the move is narrow.
2026-11-13: QQQ -1.2%, SPY -0.4%: an ordinary day.
2026-11-13: VIX fell from 25.6 to 19.3 in 5 sessions: fear easing, now normal.
2026-11-12: AVGO +25.0%: GOOGL news: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google.
2026-11-05: MU -17.5%: 'Wall Street sheds $3.2tn as tech-heavy Nasdaq plunges'; VIX 16.6 -> 28.2.
QQQ has lagged SPY by 3.1 points over 20 sessions.
SMH has lagged QQQ by 5.6 points over 20 sessions.
AAPL, NVDA, MSFT and the other largest QQQ holdings account for about 51% of its -4.2% move over 20 sessions (partial: the top 9 holdings we have prices for, 44% of the fund).
QQQ 200-day average $681.20: +$1.31 (+0.19%) from the $679.89 close. Above it, the long-term trend counts as up. A close below it would put the long-term trend down.
QQQ 1-month low $647.05: −$32.84 (-4.83%) from the $679.89 close. Staying above it means the recent low is holding. A close below it would set a new 1-month low: the decline would be continuing.

QQQ 50-day average $717.72: +$37.83 (+5.56%) from the $679.89 close. A close above it would put the short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's 'QQQ above its 50-day average' check. Below it, the short-term trend stays down; setups keep failing the pipeline's market check.
QQQ 1-month high $725.61: +$45.72 (+6.72%) from the $679.89 close. A close above it would mean the pullback is fully recovered. Below it, the pullback is not yet recovered.
SPY 50-day average $764.09: +$9.72 (+1.29%) from the $754.37 close. A close above it would put the short-term trend back up. Below it, the short-term trend stays down.
None approved. Nothing has a proven edge yet, so every setup stops at check 7 at the latest. Approving only records your decision; nothing is traded.

AAPL: No action. The strongest point against the current negative lean: Sales beat expectations; supports the growth story if it repeats. Would change the view: a close above 356.27 (breakout) or below 331.90 (breakdown); market conditions improving to GREEN.

NVDA: No action. The strongest point against the current neutral lean: Operating margin 65% sits at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%); peaks like this usually fade. Would change the view: a close above 221.97 (breakout) or below 162.85 (breakdown); market conditions improving to GREEN; the earnings report.

AMZN: No action. The strongest point against the current negative lean: Profitability is improving year on year. Would change the view: a close above 270.87 (breakout) or below 240.35 (breakdown); market conditions improving to GREEN.
